title: Open subgroups and finite etale covers
statement: Let $Y$ be a connected scheme [def-weil-connected-scheme] with a geometric point $\bar y$, and put $G=\pi_1(Y,\bar y)$ [def-galois-fibre-functor]. Finite etale covers and their geometric fibres are as in [def-galois-categories]. The assignment sending a nonempty connected finite etale cover $P\to Y$ to the conjugacy class of $\operatorname{Stab}_G(p)$, for any $p\in |P_{\bar y}|$, is a well-defined bijection between isomorphism classes of such covers and conjugacy classes of open subgroups of $G$. More precisely, isomorphism classes of pointed nonempty connected finite etale covers $(P,p)$ of $Y$, with $p\in |P_{\bar y}|$ and isomorphisms required to carry the marked geometric-fibre point to the marked point, correspond bijectively to individual open subgroups by $(P,p)\mapsto\operatorname{Stab}_G(p)$. In both forms the degree of $P\to Y$ (its constant finite locally free rank [def-pc-finite-locally-free]) equals $[G:\operatorname{Stab}_G(p)]$.

proof.text: Write $S=|P_{\bar y}|$. By [thm-galois-fundamental] the fibre functor is an equivalence to finite continuous $G$-sets. If $P$ is connected as a scheme, [lem-galois-finite-etale-connected-object] makes it a connected object, in the sense of [def-galois-connected-object]. An equivalence preserves and reflects initial objects and monomorphisms (apply its quasi-inverse), so $S$ is nonempty and has no proper nonempty invariant subset: the inclusion of any invariant subset is a monomorphism. Each orbit is such a subset, hence the action on $S$ is transitive.

Conversely suppose $S$ is a nonempty transitive finite continuous $G$-set and choose a cover $P$ representing it by essential surjectivity of [thm-galois-fundamental]. For a clopen subset $V\subseteq P$, [lem-galois-coproduct-copies-morphisms-clopen] with $U=Y$ and $E=\{0,1\}$ gives a $Y$-morphism $P\to Y\amalg Y$ whose two inverse images are $V$ and its complement. The equivalence preserves the terminal object and this coproduct, so its fibre is an equivariant map from $S$ to the trivial two-point set. Transitivity forces the map to be constant. Faithfulness then identifies the morphism with one of the two structural coprojection maps; clause (c) of the clopen-decomposition lemma says $V$ is empty or all of $P$. A chosen point of $S=|P_{\bar y}|$ projects to a point of $P$, so $P$ is nonempty. Thus $P$ is connected by [def-weil-connected-scheme].

For a point $p$ in the transitive fibre, let $H=\{g\in G:gp=p\}$. The map $g\mapsto gp$ is continuous to the discrete set $S$ [def-galois-fibre-functor], so $H$ is open. The map $G/H\to S$, $gH\mapsto gp$, is well-defined; $gp=g'p$ holds exactly when $g^{-1}g'\in H$, proving injectivity, and transitivity proves surjectivity. It is equivariant and sends $H$ to $p$. Hence $\#S=[G:H]$.

For any open subgroup $H\leq G$, the left cosets $gH$ form a disjoint open cover of the compact group $G$ (the fundamental group is profinite by [thm-galois-fundamental]); a finite subcover therefore contains every coset. Thus $G/H$ is finite. Give it the discrete topology. The inverse image of $bH$ under $g\mapsto gaH$ is $bHa^{-1}$, an open subset; since $G\times(G/H)$ is the disjoint union of the open slices $G\times\{aH\}$, this proves continuity of the action. The action is transitive and the stabilizer of $H$ is exactly $H$. Steps 1-2 and the equivalence [thm-galois-fundamental] therefore realize this pointed $G$-set by a pointed connected cover.

The equivalence [thm-galois-fundamental] identifies pointed cover isomorphisms with equivariant fibre bijections preserving the marked point. Such a bijection preserves its stabilizer. Conversely, if two pointed fibres have stabilizer $H$, the bijections in step 3 identify both, with their marked points, with $(G/H,H)$; fullness lifts their composite and its inverse to cover morphisms, and faithfulness makes both composites identities. The resulting cover isomorphism preserves the marked points, and is unique by faithfulness. This proves the pointed classification. Changing the marked point from $p$ to $ap$ changes the stabilizer from $H$ to $aHa^{-1}$, since $g(ap)=ap$ is equivalent to $a^{-1}ga\in H$. An unpointed equivariant bijection sends $p$ to some $ap'$, so its two stabilizers are conjugate. Conversely, conjugate stabilizers can be made equal by changing one marked point and then using the pointed classification. This proves precisely the unpointed classification by conjugacy classes.

For the degree assertion, a finite etale morphism is finite, flat and locally of finite presentation by [def-weil-etale-morphism], hence finite locally free by [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. Its rank function is locally constant by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-locally-free-degree-locally-constant]; the clopen rank fibres show it has one constant value $d$ on the connected nonempty base. At $y$, the image of $\bar y=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, write the finite fibre algebra as $A$ over $\kappa(y)$. A basis of $A$ stays a basis of $A\otimes_{\kappa(y)}\Omega$, so its dimension is still $d$. By [lem-galois-geometric-fibre] the geometric fibre is a disjoint union of $\#S$ copies of $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, whose algebra is $\Omega^{\#S}$, of dimension $\#S$. Thus $\deg(P/Y)=d=\#S=[G:H]$ by step 3, and conjugating $H$ does not change this index.

lean.statement: theorem connected_cover_open_subgroups {Y : Scheme.{u}} [ConnectedSpace Y] {Ω : Type u} [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (s : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ Y) : (∀ (P : Y.FiniteEtale), ConnectedSpace P.obj.left → ∀ p : (fiber s).obj P, IsOpen (MulAction.stabilizer (Aut (fiber s)) p : Set (Aut (fiber s))) ∧ P.obj.hom.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfDegree (MulAction.stabilizer (Aut (fiber s)) p).index) ∧ (∀ H : Subgroup (Aut (fiber s)), IsOpen (H : Set (Aut (fiber s))) → ∃ (P : Y.FiniteEtale), ConnectedSpace P.obj.left ∧ ∃ p : (fiber s).obj P, MulAction.stabilizer (Aut (fiber s)) p = H) ∧ (∀ (P Q : Y.FiniteEtale), ConnectedSpace P.obj.left → ConnectedSpace Q.obj.left → ∀ (p : (fiber s).obj P) (q : (fiber s).obj Q), (∃ e : P ≅ Q, (fiber s).map e.hom p = q) ↔ MulAction.stabilizer (Aut (fiber s)) p = MulAction.stabilizer (Aut (fiber s)) q) ∧ (∀ (P Q : Y.FiniteEtale), ConnectedSpace P.obj.left → ConnectedSpace Q.obj.left → ∀ (p : (fiber s).obj P) (q : (fiber s).obj Q), Nonempty (P ≅ Q) ↔ ∃ g : Aut (fiber s), ∀ h : Aut (fiber s), h ∈ MulAction.stabilizer (Aut (fiber s)) p ↔ g⁻¹ * h * g ∈ MulAction.stabilizer (Aut (fiber s)) q)
